messages.subject: question about model Gaussian mean in INLA
parts:
Hi,

I couldn't figure out how to set the mean in Gaussian/Normal likelihood in INLA. 
For example, the model I have is:
Y|mu, sigma ~ N(mu, sigma^2) where mu =alpha-beta*(gamma)^x
with prior distributions: alpha ~ Unif(0,100);  beta ~ Unif(0,100); gamma ~ Unif(0,1) and log(sigma) ~ Unif(-10,10) or 1/sigma^2 ~ Gamma(0.001,0.001)
The goal is to get the posterior summary statistics of alpha, beta, gamma, and sigma. 

I am pretty new to INLA, and my  question is how to write R-INLA code? More specifically, how to generate observations for y and x? and how to set priors for mu? how to get the posterior summaries?

FYI, the WinBugs code is
model
{
for( i in 1 : N ) {
Y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i], tau)
mu[i] <- alpha - beta * pow(gamma,x[i])
}
alpha ~ dunif(0, 100)
beta ~ dunif(0, 100)
gamma ~ dunif(0, 1)
 
tau ~ dgamma(0.001, 0.001)
sigma <- 1 / sqrt(tau)
#or log(sigma) has a uniform prior
#log.sigma ~dunif(-10,10)
#sigma<- exp(log.sigma)
#tau <- 1/pow(sigma,2)
}

Thanks a lot!! Your help is very appreciated!!
